payload.excerpt: A wedding guest list template for Excel and Google Sheets with no sign-up. Every column explained, how to fill it in by household and by event, the destination columns for flights, accommodation and visa letters, and how to share the list safely.
key_takeaways: The template downloads as an Excel file with no sign-up and opens in Excel or imports straight into Google Sheets.
Give every guest their own row and tie the people who share an invitation together with one Household ID.
Eight destination columns track where guests are flying from, their flights, dates, accommodation, transport and visa letters.
Names, addresses and phone numbers are personal information, so share the file only with the people helping you plan.

faq.q: Do you add your wedding party to your guest list?
faq.a: Yes. Everyone who will be at an event needs a row, wedding party included, because they eat, sit and travel like every other guest. Note their role in the Notes column.

faq.q: How do you make a wedding guest list in Excel?
faq.a: Put one guest per row, with a Household ID to group families, and give each event its own column. Add dropdowns for replies with data validation, freeze the header row and count replies with a formula. The template above has all of this built in, so you can start typing.

faq.q: What should you use for a wedding guest list?
faq.a: A spreadsheet suits the early months, when names are still being added and removed. Once replies are coming in, a planning app that collects them for you saves the retyping. You can use both: the spreadsheet for drafting, the app once invitations go out.

faq.q: Should a guest list have one row per person or per household?
faq.a: One row per person, grouped by a Household ID. You count meals, seats and flights by person, and invitations and envelopes by household. The template does both.

faq.q: Can I use this template in Google Sheets and Excel?
faq.a: Yes. It is an Excel file, so it opens in Excel as it is. For Google Sheets, open a spreadsheet, choose File, then Import, and select the file, then check a dropdown to make sure it came across.

faq.q: What extra columns does a destination wedding guest list need?
faq.a: Travelling from, flights booked, arrival and departure dates, accommodation, transport to the venue, and visa letter needed and sent. A separate welcome dinner column under Events helps too, because its numbers differ from the wedding's.
